To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
some calcium antagonists potentiate the depolarization- and caffeine-induced contraction in the presence of external calcium, but suppress them in the calcium-free medium.

the contractile responses of skeletal muscle to nicardipine, verapamil, or diltiazem are dependent on extracellular Ca2+ and the contractile potentiating effect of nicardipin and verapamil is not related to the inhibitory action on the caffeine contractures.

the potentiation of contractile tension by calcium antagonists is due to the increase in the number of functional calcium channels in the sarcoplasmic reticulum membrane, while the inhibitory action of these drugs on the caffeine contractures is due to the inhibition of the calcium channel at the transverse tubule membrane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the contractile potentiation of calcium antagonists.
the effects of some calcium antagonists in the skeletal muscle of the frog.
the effects of calcium antagonists in the presence and absence of external calcium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the calcium antagonists enhance the contractile tension by potentiating the calcium entry via the functional calcium channel.

the contractile potentiation of skeletal muscle induced by calcium antagonists is dependent on external calcium, whereas the inhibitory action on the caffeine contractures is independent of the calcium concentration in the bathing medium.
the potentiating effects of calcium antagonists are not related to their blocking actions on the functional calcium channel.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

calcium antagonists have dual effects in the skeletal muscle; one is to suppress the depolarization induced contracture by blocking the voltage dependent calcium channels, and the other is to potentiate the depolarization by some mechanism which does not depend on external calcium.

the potentiating action of the calcium antagonists in the depolarizing-induced contractions is caused by an increase in the amount of the calcium ions which are released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum, while the inhibitory action on the caffeine contractures is due to the direct suppression of the calcium ion release from the sarcoplamic reticulum.
calcium antagonists potentiate the contractile response to depolarization by a mechanism independent of calcium antagonism, and inhibit caffeine contracture by a calcium antagonist action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the contractile potentiation induced by calcium antagonists is dependent on extracellular calcium and that the inhibitory effect of calcium antagonists is not dependent on extracellular sodium.
calcium antagonists may have a different mode of action in skeletal muscles.
the effects of calcium antagonists depend not only on external calcium, but also on the type of calcium antagonists.
